data.text:
I just designed a website with Claude Fable 5. It launched today. And honestly, the lines between AI generated designs and human designs is blurring fast!

I run a design agency. AI generated slop makes me want to close it fast!

Fable didn't do any of that.

Real hierarchy. Intentional whitespace. Restraint. The kind of decisions you usually only see from designers who've shipped real products. No model has come close to this before. Not one.

The benchmarks back it up. 80.3% on SWE-bench Pro, where Opus 4.8 scored 69.2%. But the design output impressed me more than any number.

Here's the part worth reading twice though. Anthropic's own announcement says writing code stopped being the slow part a while ago, and that Fable pushes the bottleneck toward verification and review.

Same is now true for design.

→ Producing a beautiful screen: getting solved

→ Knowing which screen to produce, and why: not solved

→ Designing for trust, edge cases, real users with real money: not solved

→ Verifying it holds up in production: not solved

For designers and developers: production will no longer be the moat. Your taste and Judgment will be. Fable just made that very obvious.

Check it out here:
https://t.co/sMSZ1o55S8

#AI #ProductDesign #SaaS #ClaudeFable5 #DesignCraft

data.text:
Claude Fable 5 designed a robot joint in 30 minutes: motor, gearbox, housing.

It animated the gearbox and checked for part collisions before handing the design over. Demo by engineer Jake Fitzgerald, video is his.

The part isn't the story. The self-check is what CAD tools get paid for.

Spun it around in the browser viewer: output stack, motor windings, housing, an electronics board. A 4.5:1 gear reduction that actually animates.

400k tokens of design, simulate, inspect. Game clones test recall. This has to physically fit together and spin.

Fair caveat: an animation isn't a stress test, and we haven't seen the prompts end to end.

Jake shipped the whole loop as open-source skills: https://t.co/rjqX0EHMdU

The finished part is spinnable at https://t.co/wnZhoFaitj.

data.text:
Introducing Rotatron for Super Nintendo (SNES). The super addictive puzzler.

Haters gonna hate, I'm sure. But it's coming. Still optimizing, polishing.

Claude Fable 5 made it happen. Some challenging bits here, experially rotating the hexagons and getting the spaceships right. As you'll see even @elonmusk's Starship is represented :)

Claude Fable 5 has impressive spatial reasoning capabilities that are immediately relevant for engineering and design: In this example I gave Claude Fable 5 a single photo of a hierarchical mesh torus (image generated using a text-to-image model); and in one shot, no iteration, it built a full interactive 3D simulation: ~1,400 nodes & 4,400 fibers, realistic mass–spring physics you can grab, compress, twist… plus strain-based sonification so you can 'hear' the structure vibrate. It inferred the complete 3D topology from a partial 2D view. ⤵️
